messages:
From: James Delgado <j.delgado@novusbank.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 20:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Spike of 503s during nightly batch window

Sofia —

We started seeing a spike of 503s and per-request timeouts across our reconciliation jobs between ~19:52–20:07 ET last night. ~4% of nightly batches failed, and a few customer statements were delayed. Our ops team captured request IDs and a short trace; I can share those if helpful.

Can you confirm whether this was caused by anything on Redwood’s side and whether the issue is resolved? We have an open maintenance window tomorrow and need to know if we should change backoff retries or schedule.

Thanks,
James Delgado
Sr. SRE, Novus Bank
[j.delgado@novusbank.com]

Hi James —

Thanks for the alert and the log snippet — that’s very helpful. We saw elevated 5xx rates in our metrics at the same time window for the cluster serving your model variant. Our on-call started an investigation immediately.

Immediate notes: we’ve opened JIRA INF-4932 to track the incident, and Markus is preparing a technical timeline and a customer-facing summary. I’ll share a consolidated recovery summary and a proposed mitigation plan within 24 hours (by 7/14 EOD your local time).

For now, two safe short-term recommendations for your batch window:
- Increase client-side retries with exponential backoff (up to 3 attempts) for non-idempotent jobs where safe.
- If possible, stagger parallel workers by 30s to reduce simultaneous load spikes on warm cache paths.

Would you like us to join a quick sync with your ops tomorrow morning to walk through the timeline?

Best,

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: customer-facing recovery summary (technical timeline)

Sofia / Lauren —

Below is a compact technical timeline and root-cause summary for Novus Bank. This is written for a customer audience but contains the specifics your team asked for. I attached a short PDF draft (production_recovery_rca_draft.pdf) and a small log excerpt (logs_snippet.txt). Please review and flag anything that looks like privileged internal detail before we send.

Technical timeline (UTC):
- 2027-07-13 23:52:00Z — Routine model rollout (minor config change: KV cache resize) began on the primary serving pool.
- 2027-07-13 23:55:30Z — A subset of workers experienced a rapid sequence of prefix cache evictions during warmup; this triggered higher memory churn than anticipated on those containers.
- 2027-07-13 23:56:20Z — A transient kernel allocation failure caused by the eviction pattern led to local worker OOMs on ~3% of GPUs in the pool. Affected workers returned 5xx to upstream for in-flight requests while the control plane initiated replacement.
- 2027-07-13 23:56:20–00:07:00Z — Traffic was shifted to degraded capacity (fallback pool) that had higher cold-start latency and some throttling; that caused increased 503/504 responses observed by Novus.
- 2027-07-14 00:08:45Z — Hotfix deployed to stop aggressive cache eviction during rollout; autoscaler policy adjusted to favor conservative burst capacity.
- 2027-07-14 00:12:10Z — Error rates returned to baseline, and full capacity restored by 00:25Z.

Root cause (summary for customer):
- A configuration change to KV cache sizing combined with a server-side race during rollout caused unexpected cache eviction behavior. The eviction pattern increased memory pressure and triggered OOMs on a small set of workers. Those worker failures produced transient 5xx responses and caused downstream throttling while traffic was rebalanced.

Mitigations and immediate actions taken:
- Hotfix deployed to prevent aggressive eviction during rollout (applied 00:08Z).
- Increased short-term spare capacity in the affected region to reduce hot-path throttling.
- Autoscaler conservative thresholds restored and rollout window controls added to the deployment pipeline.

Planned follow-ups (owner / ETA):
- Permanent fix to the eviction algorithm and rollout orchestration — owner: infra/serving (Markus) — targeted release: 2027-08-01.
- Additional e2e load test cases for cache warmup scenarios — owner: reliability eng (Lauren) — targeted 2027-07-28.
- Dashboard alert tuning and added synthetic checks for cache warmup latency — owner: observability (SRE) — targeted 2027-07-21.

Attachments referenced: production_recovery_rca_draft.pdf (customer-facing PDF), logs_snippet.txt (redacted trace lines).

Markus
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Hi James —

Thank you again for the quick signal and the log traces you shared. Attached is a concise, customer-facing summary of what happened, the timeline, and our commitments ("customer_summary_v1.pdf"). Below is the in-email summary in case you prefer to keep it in thread:

Summary (short):
- What happened: During a routine rollout on 2027-07-13 we observed an unexpected cache eviction pattern that briefly increased memory pressure on a small set of GPU workers. Those workers returned 5xx errors, and traffic was briefly routed to a degraded fallback pool, resulting in elevated 503/504 responses for ~15 minutes.
- Impact: ~4% of nightly reconciliation batches experienced failures between 19:52–20:07 ET; no data loss reported.
- What we did: applied a hotfix to stop aggressive eviction, increased spare capacity, and adjusted autoscaler behavior to prevent recurrence.

Customer-facing action items and timeline:
1) Short-term: We recommend continuing with the staggered-worker approach and 3 retry attempts as discussed; Redwood will provide a recommended client retry configuration by 7/16. (Owner: Sofia / ETA: 2027-07-16)
2) Medium-term: Permanent fix to eviction algorithm and rollout orchestration (owner: Markus). ETA: 2027-08-01.
3) Reliability testing: Additional load tests and synthetic checks to catch cache-warmup regressions (owner: Lauren). ETA: 2027-07-28.
4) Follow-up sync: Proposed call on 2027-07-21 10:00 ET to review progress and confirm mitigations; please let me know if that works for your team.

We’d also like to offer a one-time account credit for the impact window; I can route that through your account rep if you accept.

Attachments: customer_summary_v1.pdf (concise timeline and commitments), production_recovery_rca_draft.pdf (technical appendix), logs_snippet.txt (redacted).

Please reply with any questions or if you’d like us to broaden the postmortem distribution list. If you’re ok, we’ll publish the public postmortem link (https://redwood.example.com/postmortems/2027-07-14-prod-interruption) and share the permanent fix ticket (JIRA-INF-4932) after you review.

Thanks,
